name: Can interior walls and ceilings be attached directly to the metal building frame?
description: Interior framing is typically anchored to the slab or attached via engineered non-rigid clips; never cut or drill into primary rigid frames without engineering

mainEntity.name: Can interior walls and ceilings be attached directly to the metal building frame?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cutting or drilling into primary structural frames or rigid rafters is generally prohibited, as it compromises the engineered load capacity of the building shell. Pre-engineered steel buildings are designed to carry specific live, dead, wind, and seismic loads. Instead of altering primary frames, contractors attach interior walls using light-gauge tracks secured to the concrete slab, floating clips on secondary purlins, or self-supporting ceiling joist systems. If you must hang heavy mechanical units or build a mezzanine, an engineer must review the framing plans to verify whether reinforcement or dedicated posts are necessary.
acceptedAnswer.description: Interior framing is typically anchored to the slab or attached via engineered non-rigid clips; never cut or drill into primary rigid frames without engineering approval.
